15/20 mg WITH food; 2.5/10 mg with or without

summary: Rivaroxaban is an oral direct factor Xa inhibitor used for stroke prevention in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, treatment and recurrence-reduction of DVT/PE, post-orthopedic and medical VTE prophylaxis, and (with aspirin) cardiovascular risk reduction in CAD/PAD. It carries TWO boxed warnings: (A) premature discontinuation increases the risk of thrombotic events such as stroke - bridge with another anticoagulant if stopped early; and (B) spinal/epidural hematoma in patients undergoing neuraxial anesthesia or spinal puncture, which can cause long-term or permanent paralysis. There is no routine coagulation monitoring and no widely stocked reversal agent.
indications: Reduce risk of stroke and systemic embolism in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
Reduction in risk of recurrence of DVT and/or PE after >=6 months of treatment
Prophylaxis of DVT following hip or knee replacement surgery
Prophylaxis of VTE in acutely ill medical patients not at high risk of bleeding
Reduce risk of major cardiovascular events in CAD (with aspirin)
Reduce risk of major thrombotic vascular events in PAD, including after lower extremity revascularization (with aspirin)
Treatment and recurrence reduction of VTE in pediatric patients birth to <18 years
Thromboprophylaxis in pediatric patients >=2 years with congenital heart disease after Fontan procedure

dosage.n: Reduce to 15 mg once daily if CrCl <=50 mL/min

Once daily, 6-10 h post-op after hemostasis

dosage.n: Not for patients at high risk of bleeding

dosage.t: Twice daily, with or without food

admin: Take 15 mg and 20 mg tablets WITH food to ensure adequate absorption
2.5 mg and 10 mg tablets may be taken with or without food
For atrial fibrillation, take 20 mg (or 15 mg) once daily with the evening meal
May crush tablet and mix in applesauce or give via NG tube if needed; give immediately
Do NOT discontinue prematurely without alternative anticoagulant coverage (boxed warning A)
Avoid neuraxial procedures unless anticoagulant effect is low; remove indwelling catheter only after >=2 half-lives (boxed warning B)
moa: Rivaroxaban is a selective direct inhibitor of factor Xa that does not require antithrombin III as a cofactor. It inhibits both free factor Xa and prothrombinase activity, thereby decreasing thrombin generation. It has no direct effect on platelet aggregation but indirectly inhibits thrombin-induced platelet aggregation, producing dose-dependent anticoagulation.

absolute: Severe hypersensitivity reaction to rivaroxaban (e.g., anaphylaxis)
relative: Moderate to severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B/C) or hepatic disease with coagulopathy
Pregnancy (use only if benefit justifies risk)
monitor: BOXED WARNING A: premature discontinuation increases thrombotic event (stroke) risk - cover with another anticoagulant if stopped early
BOXED WARNING B: neuraxial anesthesia / spinal puncture / indwelling epidural catheter - risk of spinal-epidural hematoma and permanent paralysis; monitor frequently for neurological impairment
Concomitant combined P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors/inducers
Concomitant antiplatelets, NSAIDs, or other anticoagulants

preg: Limited data are insufficient to characterize drug-associated risk. Use with caution because of potential for pregnancy-related hemorrhage and/or emergent delivery; the anticoagulant effect cannot be reliably monitored with standard laboratory testing. Factor Xa inhibitors may cross the placenta and bleeding may occur in the fetus/neonate. Weigh maternal benefit against fetal risk.
lact: Rivaroxaban has been detected in human milk; data are insufficient to determine effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Consider developmental/health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: Exposure increases ~44-64% with renal impairment. Atrial fibrillation: 15 mg once daily if CrCl <=50 mL/min. DVT/PE treatment, recurrence reduction, orthopedic and medical prophylaxis: avoid if CrCl <15 mL/min and observe closely if CrCl 15 to <30 mL/min. Reassess renal function periodically; consider dose adjustment or discontinuation if acute renal failure develops.
hepatic: AUC increases ~127% in moderate (Child-Pugh B) impairment. Avoid use in patients with moderate or severe (Child-Pugh B/C) hepatic impairment or any hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy due to increased exposure and bleeding risk. Not evaluated in severe hepatic impairment.

major: Combined P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, ritonavir) - increase rivaroxaban exposure and bleeding risk; avoid
Combined P-gp and strong CYP3A inducers (carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampin, St. John's wort) - decrease exposure and increase thrombotic risk; avoid
Other anticoagulants (warfarin, enoxaparin, heparins) - avoid concurrent use due to bleeding risk
moderate: Antiplatelets (aspirin, clopidogrel, P2Y12 inhibitors, dual antiplatelet therapy) - increased bleeding
Combined P-gp and moderate CYP3A inhibitors (erythromycin) in CrCl 15 to <80 mL/min - avoid unless benefit justifies risk
SSRIs and SNRIs - increased bleeding risk
minor: Clarithromycin - combined P-gp/strong CYP3A inhibitor but no precautions needed
Drugs altering gastric pH (ranitidine, antacids, omeprazole) - no effect on exposure
interactions.food: 15 mg and 20 mg doses must be taken with food (food increases 20 mg bioavailability, AUC +39%, Cmax +76%); 2.5 mg and 10 mg unaffected by food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excessive alcohol; may add to bleeding risk and impair hepatic function.
interactions.diagnostics: Prolongs PT, aPTT and anti-factor Xa activity dose-dependently; routine coagulation monitoring is not recommended.

common: Cough, vomiting and gastroenteritis (most common in pediatrics, >10%)
serious: Major bleeding including intracranial and gastrointestinal hemorrhage
Thrombotic events (including stroke) after premature discontinuation
Reduced effect / recurrent thrombosis in triple-positive antiphospholipid syndrome
emergency: BOXED WARNING B: spinal/epidural hematoma - midline back pain, lower-limb numbness/tingling/weakness, bowel or bladder dysfunction; can progress to permanent paralysis - seek urgent care
Major or fatal hemorrhage (intracranial, GI; severe headache, hematemesis, melena, hypotension)
BOXED WARNING A: stroke or thrombosis after stopping drug abruptly

monitoring: Signs and symptoms of bleeding; hemoglobin/hematocrit and blood pressure
Renal function periodically (more often when decline expected) and adjust therapy
Frequent neurological assessment for signs of spinal/epidural hematoma in patients with neuraxial anesthesia or indwelling catheter
Routine coagulation testing (PT, INR, aPTT, anti-FXa) is NOT recommended
counsel: Do not stop taking rivaroxaban without talking to your provider - stopping early raises the risk of stroke or clots
Take 15 mg and 20 mg doses with food at the same time each day
Report any unusual bleeding or bruising, red/black stools, coughing or vomiting blood promptly
Tell your provider immediately about back pain, leg numbness/weakness, or loss of bladder/bowel control, especially after spinal anesthesia or a spinal tap
Inform all providers and dentists that you take an anticoagulant before any procedure or surgery
pk: Anticoagulant effect within 2-4 h of intake
Once or twice daily dosing per indication
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); do not freeze granules/suspension
pearls: TWO boxed warnings: (A) premature discontinuation increases thrombotic/stroke risk - bridge with another anticoagulant; (B) spinal/epidural hematoma with neuraxial procedures can cause permanent paralysis
15 mg and 20 mg tablets MUST be taken with food; low 2.5/10 mg doses are not food-dependent
No routine coagulation monitoring required; no reliable lab assay for effect
Not dialyzable due to high (92-95%) protein binding; no widely stocked specific reversal agent
Avoid in CrCl <15 mL/min, moderate/severe hepatic impairment, prosthetic valves, and triple-positive APS
missed: For once-daily regimens, take the missed dose immediately the same day and resume the normal schedule the next day; do not double up. For the 15 mg twice-daily phase, take immediately to ensure 30 mg per day (two 15 mg tablets may be taken together) then resume normal twice-daily dosing. For 2.5 mg twice daily, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule.
overdose: Overdose may cause hemorrhage. Discontinue rivaroxaban and provide supportive care. Absorption is limited above single doses of 50 mg; activated charcoal may reduce absorption. Not dialyzable due to high protein binding. Partial reversal of lab parameters may be achieved with plasma products (PCC, aPCC, recombinant factor VIIa may be considered); no specific anti-factor Xa reversal agent is included in this label.
